%1$s) Privacy policy
Tap to read the privacy policy

Dear users,
We are committed to improving the app, and for that we need to collect errors and crashes.
Errors and crashes differ between devices and Android versions, so we collect them together with the Android version and device type. This happens automatically, only while you use the app, through a third-party cloud service.
By studying how people use the app we can also improve it step by step.
For errors and crashes we collect things like the type and time of the error, the Android version and the device type; the full list is in the privacy policy linked below.
For usage we collect things like how long the app is used, the user's country and city and the device maker; the full list is in the privacy policy linked below.
As explained above, using the app means you accept the privacy policy.
Smart learning
Part 1: Brain circuits\nPart 2: How the app works\nPart 3: A roadmap for memorizing words
Part 1: Brain circuits
This app is designed around how the brain learns and forms circuits, so we start with a short look at how that works.
The brain, a miracle
The brain has billions of cells, and learning happens when a path between cells is built or strengthened. A new path forms a brain circuit, like this:
When learning starts, electrical pulses try to cross from one cell to another, but there is a gap between them:
With repetition the pulses grow stronger until the gap is bridged, a new circuit is built and learning happens:
There is much more to say about the brain, but this short introduction is enough for now.
Part 2: How the app works
We built the app around this ability of the brain, and split repetition into two stages that bring a word into memory:
%1$s) Into short-term memory\n%2$s) Into long-term memory
How the two stages work in the app
%1$s) Into short-term memory:
This stage is the Learn button on each lesson page, which runs the learning algorithm:

Each lesson has %1$s words, taught in three groups of four. %2$s words are ready to learn at a time; when their steps are finished, the next %2$s words are ready.\nThe algorithm repeats them in a smart, automatic order that works best for short-term memory.\nWe suggest you focus on the words at this stage and leave the example sentences for later.
%1$s) Into long-term memory:

This stage is the "Fast review", at three levels:
 - Fast review of each lesson
 - Fast review of each class
 - Fast review of each class's difficult words

A lesson review repeats %1$s words and takes %2$s to %3$s seconds.\nA class review covers several lessons at once: any number of the class\'s %4$s lessons, quickly and together. It can have %5$s to %6$s words.
Part 3: A roadmap for memorizing words
Getting a word into memory means building a circuit for it, and that takes repetition, repetition and repetition.\n\nThe roadmap is simple:

Step 1:
Fully learn each lesson's words
(reset words and learn again if needed)

Step 2:
Fast review each lesson (many times)

Step 3:
With each new lesson learned, fast review the class (many times)

Step 4:
Mark difficult words and fast review them (many times)

And once more:
repeat, repeat, repeat
or in other words
fast review, fast review, fast review
